parts.text: When you sit down to plan a flight, where do the details of the job come from?
Can you give me a concrete example of the kinds of restrictions a site, load, or customer might put on a flight?
What do you check by hand today before signing off, because you don't trust what the current system tells you?
Think back over the last few months—what was the worst day you had on the desk, and what made it so bad?
When something goes wrong with a flight or a drone in the middle of operations, what do you need to know right away?
Walk me through everyone you hand work to, or who hands work to you, over the course of a shift.
What are you most afraid a new shared service would do wrong?
Earlier you mentioned checking by hand whether a drone is really ready and whether another dispatcher has grabbed it or a landing spot—how do you actually do those checks today?
Once you sign off and a flight leaves, what do you actually do while it is in the air until it arrives?
What makes handing over the desk to the next dispatcher at the end of a shift go well or badly?
When airspace rules change during your shift, how does that information reach you today, and how do you figure out which of your flights it affects?
